I am disgusted and disturbed by the astounding number of people who bring their dogs off leash. Furthermore - not a single one of those people have a dog, or often a few dogs, with ANY recall. First and foremost - you are a danger to yourself, you put your pet in danger, and you put every single other person on that trail in danger, when you DO NOT have a solidly trained dog with 100% recall. More to the point - when someone asks you to leash your dog, and they are holding onto their own leashed, and haltered, dog - it is 100% for a legitimate reason - and that reason is usually for you and your dogs safety. So when you blatantly say no, or "we're good" and completely ignore that persons VERY reasonable (and LEGALLY BINDING) request, yet your dog with ZERO recall comes running at my dog - when your dog gets bit - you only have yourself to blame. No one got bit or attacked today - but please be a reasonable human being and a responsible dog owner and simply leash your dog for the time it takes for the not friendly and reactive dog in exposure training to pass safely and with no anxiety - because that is what you are enciting by not leashing your not at all trained dog. Be smart people - use your head.

There were often multiple dogs per person. I tried to give them lots of room and warning that I was coming but almost nobody made any effort to control their dogs. I have had as many as three dogs at a time of my own and am not an animal-hater but I think it is really important to respect other people's comfort levels and to control your pet. Just be aware of this if you plan to hike here and it is something that makes you uncomfortable.

Very frustrating first time here. I took another reviewer’s advice and am so glad - I used the GPS but spent far too much time looking at the GPS trying to stay on the 10km loop. The most travelled trails philosophy didn’t work here as there were a gazillion trails all worn the same way. Almost no trail signage which was just mind boggling. Not even colours painted on trees to help guide you on a particular route. There were lots of people with dogs, which was wonderful and everyone was super friendly, it was just very unnecessarily frustrating trying to stay on the route. Maybe it would be better the second time out but I won’t go back here again as there are other places to go where routes are clearly marked and it’s more fun than frustration.
